data.narrative: Alekhya demonstrated superior proficiency with performance debugging and profiling tools throughout Module 04. She correctly prioritized runtime observation over static code inspection, diagnosing Bug #6 (connection handle leaks on exception paths) and Bug #7 (N+1 query regression caused by silent ORM eager loading default changes). In the BREAK challenge, she immediately diagnosed ReDoS catastrophic backtracking, replacing nested regex quantifiers with linear O(n) URL parser validation.

dimension_scores.observation: Reasoned through APM integration vs manual profiling, selecting manual runtime tools for zero-cost, zero-overhead targeted local diagnostic precision
dimension_scores.evidence: Manual profiling with runtime tools gives full local control with zero overhead and zero vendor cost to isolate N+1 queries and connection leaks directly at the source.

dimension_scores.observation: Refused to guess or rely on blueprint code reading, using memory snapshots and SQL query logs to prove runtime behavior
dimension_scores.evidence: Used tracemalloc to verify connection handle stability (delta 297KB across 500 requests) and SQL query logging to expose 51 queries collapsed to 2 batch queries.

dimension_scores.observation: Understood that services can return 100% correct responses while catastrophically failing on latency and resource starvation
dimension_scores.evidence: N+1 queries returned correct data but took 3,000ms+; unclosed connections on error paths exhausted pool handles after 2,000 requests. Observability must inspect runtime resource consumption.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified and neutralized ReDoS catastrophic backtracking attack vectors, enforcing linear O(n) parsing and input bounds
dimension_scores.evidence: ReDoS nested quantifiers attempt exponential O(2^n) permutations on mismatched endings. Replaced vulnerable regex with urllib.parse.urlsplit to drop latency from 47s to 22ms.

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered razor-sharp technical explanations with clear database and profiler evidence
dimension_scores.evidence: Demonstrated that finally: conn.close() guarantees socket cleanup on exception branches, and selectinload replaces N+1 loops with single batch joins.

strengths: Runtime profiler mastery: uses heap snapshots and query logging to discover bugs invisible to static code reviews.
Root-cause remediation: fixes N+1 queries at the database layer via eager loading rather than applying superficial caching band-aids.
Algorithmic security awareness: immediately recognizes catastrophic regex backtracking and replaces it with linear O(n) parsers.
growth_areas: Preparing for real-time high-stress incident response and stakeholder management in Module 05: Incident Response Under Pressure.
data.recommendation: Advance to Module 05: Incident Response Under Pressure.

public_evidence.student_action: Fixed connection pool leak with unconditional finally cleanup and eliminated N+1 query loop using selectinload eager loading.
public_evidence.technical_detail: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2.0 selectinload + PostgreSQL 16 + tracemalloc + cProfile
public_evidence.proof: Memory delta stabilized to 297KB across 500 requests; /api/admin/links latency dropped from 3,000ms+ to 7.04ms (2 queries instead of 51); ReDoS payload resolved in 22ms
public_evidence.ability: Performance profiling, connection pool lifecycle management, ORM query optimization, and ReDoS hardening
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates critical production diagnostics: profiling runtime performance, eliminating N+1 database bottlenecks, and hardening APIs against resource exhaustion
